presentingComplaint: Easy bruising and a spreading rash of tiny red spots on the legs for the past 5 days
history: Previously well 32-year-old woman presents with a 5-day history of spontaneous bruising, a non-blanching pinpoint rash over both shins, bleeding gums when brushing teeth, and one episode of epistaxis that stopped with pressure. Menstrual period this month was heavier than usual. Reports a mild viral upper respiratory illness roughly 2 weeks ago that has since resolved. No fever, weight loss, night sweats or bone pain. No new medications, no heparin exposure, no recent quinine/quinidine, no herbal supplements. No alcohol excess, no family history of bleeding disorders. No recent travel to a dengue/malaria-endemic area.
examination: Alert and well-appearing, not toxic. Scattered petechiae over both lower legs and buccal mucosa, with several ecchymoses on the forearms. Wet purpura noted on the palate. No lymphadenopathy. No hepatosplenomegaly on careful palpation. No joint swelling, no sternal tenderness. No signs of active major bleeding; fundi normal; no focal neurology.

labs.Peripheral smear: Reduced platelet number with occasional large platelets; no schistocytes, blasts or clumping

imaging: Not indicated for classic uncomplicated presentation; abdominal ultrasound (if performed) shows no splenomegaly
citations: Harrison 22e - Disorders of Platelets and Vessel Wall (Thrombocytopenia)
contraindications: Avoid platelet transfusion unless life-threatening bleeding (rapid consumption; reserve for ICH or major hemorrhage)
Caution with corticosteroids in undiagnosed infection or poorly controlled diabetes
Avoid NSAIDs/antiplatelet agents and IM injections while thrombocytopenic
edgeCases: Normal smear and isolated thrombocytopenia is the rule - presence of schistocytes should redirect to TTP/HUS, and blasts or cytopenias in other lineages to leukaemia
Secondary ITP (HIV, HCV, SLE, H. pylori) must be excluded before labelling primary
EDTA-induced pseudothrombocytopenia: repeat count in citrate tube if smear shows clumping
expectedMaiK: Isolated severe thrombocytopenia with a normal smear (no schistocytes/blasts), normal coagulation, and mucocutaneous bleeding in an otherwise well young adult is classic for primary ITP - a diagnosis of exclusion. Prioritise ruling out TTP, leukaemia and DIC, and treat with corticosteroids +/- IVIG given the very low count.
expectedNextQuestions: Any recent new drugs, quinine, heparin or vaccinations?
Any features of TTP (fever, confusion, focal neurology) or systemic illness (weight loss, bone pain, night sweats)?
expectedInvestigations: Peripheral blood smear review to exclude schistocytes/blasts/clumping
HIV, HCV and hepatitis B serology; consider ANA and H. pylori testing
regressionAssertions: differential should include ttp_hus and acute_leukemia
